subject: MSA + Order Form redlines: indemnity scope and evidence routing
messages:
From: Allison Park <allison.park@novacare.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: NovaCare Procurement <procurement@novacare.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: MSA redlines: indemnity + evidence ask (attached)

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for taking this. Attached is NovaCare's redline of the MSA and the draft order form showing the indemnity positions we need to be comfortable with for a formal internal procurement approval. High level: they want (a) Redwood to defend & indemnify for third-party IP claims arising from use of the service by NovaCare customers, (b) clarity around what counts as "evidence" and timing for notice, and (c) insurance/escrow triggers if claims exceed a threshold.

Specific asks we need answered for procurement:
- Do you accept defend-or-reimburse for claims alleging infringement of third-party IP caused by outputs generated by the model?
- Can Redwood commit to a 30-day notice/response SLA and a named technical liaison for evidence collection?
- Any objections to an escrow-trigger at $1M, with insurer offset language?

We've highlighted the problematic carveouts in yellow (training-data claims, claims based on customer-provided prompts). If you could come back with your preferred options and any alternative compromise language by Monday EOD, we can route to legal procurement.

Thanks — happy to set a call.

Best,
Allison Park
Sr. Counsel, NovaCare
Allison.Park@novacare.com

Attachment: NovaCare_MSA_Redline_20260821.pdf (redline PDF, 12 pages)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Allison Park <allison.park@novacare.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines: indemnity + evidence ask (attached)

Allison —

Appreciate the detailed notes. Looping in Kimberly (legal) and Ben (legal ops) to scope an operational response. Quick read: NovaCare's stance is broadly aligned with deals we can do, but we need to tighten the notice/evidence mechanics and preserve carveouts for training-data claims and service-leveling for operational feasibility.

Proposed path (high level):
1) Redwood will defend & indemnify for third-party IP claims that directly allege the service output infringes third-party IP, subject to notice, cooperation, and Redwood control of defense.
2) Carveout: claims relating to the model training corpus or the provenance of pre-2020 datasets remain excluded (we can discuss narrow exceptions).
3) Evidence and liaison: Redwood will provide a named technical liaison and a read-only evidence bucket for sample outputs; NovaCare must supply claim materials and access to the customer interaction logs required to reproduce the output.
4) Escrow/insurance: agree to an escrow trigger at a threshold, but ask NovaCare to accept insurer-offset and subrogation rights.

Kimberly — can you draft a short alternative clause we can send back? Ben — can you confirm whether ops can meet a 30-day evidence SLA and where we land on escrow mechanics?

If this looks OK to NovaCare, we should do a 30-minute sync early next week to finalize tradeoffs.

Thanks,
Rachel
Director, Legal Operations, Redwood Inference

(Thanks — I'll upload a draft response doc.)

From: Allison Park <allison.park@novacare.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: NovaCare Procurement <procurement@novacare.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 08:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines: indemnity + evidence ask (attached)

Rachel / team —

Thanks for the quick reply and the proposed approach. Procurement's key constraints: they need defense for third-party claims to avoid downstream exposure to our customers; they are open to limited carveouts but we cannot accept a broad training-data exclusion that would swallow operational risk. A couple clarifications:

- On "defend & indemnify": NovaCare expects Redwood to take primary defense when the claim arises from end-user use of the service (i.e., customer prompts -> model output). We are open to letting Redwood control defense but require frequent status updates and rights to select counsel if there's a conflict.
- On evidence: procurement insists that "evidence" includes (1) the output in question, (2) the customer prompt chain, and (3) application logs sufficient to reproduce the output. They note you may not have retained prompts in all cases; please confirm retention windows.
- On escrow/insurance: procurement can agree to insurer offset, but asks for a lower escrow trigger of $750k given their risk profile.

If you can provide redline language for the defend clause and confirmation of retention windows, procurement will evaluate the escrow threshold change. Let's schedule a call — can you do Tue 10–11am PT?

Allison
Sr. Counsel, NovaCare

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Allison Park <allison.park@novacare.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 09:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Redwood proposed language — limited defend for third-party output claims

Allison / Rachel —

Per Rachel's ask, attached is Redwood's proposed alternative clause (short form below). We aimed to strike a balance between NovaCare procurement's need for primary defense and Redwood's concerns about training-data and discovery burden.

Redwood proposed short clause (excerpt):
"Redwood will defend and indemnify Customer against any third-party claim that the direct output produced by the Service, when used by Customer in accordance with the Documentation, infringes a third party's patent, copyright or trademark, provided that Customer: (a) notifies Redwood promptly in writing and provides the evidence reasonably available to Customer to reproduce the output (including prompt chain and relevant application logs); (b) provides Redwood with sole control of the defense and settlement, subject to Customer's right to approve any settlement that does not include a full release of Customer; and (c) does not assert claims arising from Redwood's training data, models, or third-party components used in model development."

Operational points:
- Retention: Redwood retains request/response logs for 90 days by default; longer retention windows are available as a paid add-on. If NovaCare needs a 180-day window for retention, we'll need to document that in the order form.
- Escrow / threshold: Redwood can accept an escrow trigger but requests insurer-offset and subrogation assignment; Redwood proposes $1M but can move to $750k if NovaCare accepts a 3:1 notification & cure period and promotes an early mediation step.

Attachment: Redwood_proposed_indemnity_V1.docx (editable clause, 2 pages)

If that draft is workable, let's lock the meeting Tue 10am PT and finalize.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Allison Park <allison.park@novacare.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: NovaCare Procurement <procurement@novacare.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood proposed language — limited defend for third-party output claims

Kimberly / Rachel —

Thanks — the draft is much closer. Procurement accepts 90-day logs if Redwood confirms a path to 180 days as an order-form addon (we can budget for that). NovaCare will accept the $1M trigger only if Redwood will accept insurer-offset language and an explicit early mediation step; if you move to $750k and quick mediation, procurement will probably greenlight.

I've sent a calendar invite for Tue 10:00–10:30am PT to finalize tradeoffs and get procurement signoff. Agenda: agree defend clause language, confirm retention/paid addon terms, finalize escrow/threshold and mediation cadence.

See you Tuesday —
Allison
